summary: Plumas NF lookout planned in 1931, reported as a 60-foot steel tower in 1934, staffed through the 1960s; both FFLA lists mark it Standing* (cab no longer in place), and its current condition is unconfirmed.

facts.design: Steel tower, reported as 60 feet in 1934 and 50 feet in a 1951 item
facts.status_note: Both FFLA lists mark it Standing*, meaning the structure is kept with its cab no longer in place. Current condition unconfirmed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Both FFLA lists read Standing* for Red Hill in Plumas. The legend defines the mark as a tower that keeps its structure with the cab no longer in place. The Gone entry above it in the statewide list belongs to Rattlesnake (Del Norte), not Red Hill.

notes_for_editor: Height conflict: 1934 item says 60-foot steel tower (matches record 18.3 m); 1951 item says 50-foot tower. Not resolved. Status: both FFLA lists read Standing* (cab no longer in place, per legend). An earlier note that the statewide list read Gone was wrong. No source after 1964 for the tower; two web searches found only other Red Hill towers and nothing for Plumas. Staffing history is well sourced from several newspaper clippings transcribed on the Forest Lookouts page (Feather River Bulletin, Indian Valley Record, Plumas Independent, Nevada State Journal, Portola Reporter). No photos found. Do not encourage climbing.
